note: The furthest outside the stated ICP of anyone in this batch, and the closest to the definition's own explicit exclusion. Misses successful: a municipal Parks and Recreation grounds manager, not a business owner, physician or equivalent. Misses income decisively and by the widest margin in the corpus — $40 of cash on hand, earmarked for fuel, against a mortgage, a credit card being paid down and a retirement-account repayment with a two-year horizon. Misses good_to_great: this is rescue, not optimisation — 220 lb at 5'11", a 36-inch waist he wants down to 30, 'I would like to have core muscles', and 'Embarrassed of having this gut hanging out front.' Misses not_deconditioned, and this is the finding: the stated ICP excludes 'dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight, who are just like, I need to just lose weight and I hate working out', and this prospect describes his own weight as 'technically obese', is roughly 30 to 40 lb above his own target, does not train, and avoids gyms both from shyness and from being filmed by other members. He is close to the literal negative example the ICP was written to exclude, and he still received a fifty-five minute closer call. Matches neglected_health, the one criterion that holds, and it holds awkwardly: health is unmistakably the neglected domain of his life, but the presentation is closer to the crisis end than the criterion contemplates — Ehlers-Danlos syndrome with recurrent shoulder and kneecap subluxation, daily pain, and ice packs after work. Recorded as a match on the same reading applied to the Francisco Vega assessment, with the caveat noted. The broader observation this row supports: the stated ICP has no clinical criterion, and it also has no screening mechanism attached to any of its criteria, so a prospect who fails four of five can still consume a full closing slot. Judged on criteria, not outcome — and here the two agree, which is the exception in this batch rather than the rule.
